Follow the sequence **Tuesday lecture → Thursday guided practice → graded lab**. Use Canvas for official assignments and deadlines.

The topics below are tentative planning slots, not calendar dates. Links appear only when materials are available. The syllabus and confirmed schedule will be provided through Canvas.

## Available introductory materials

These examples are available to explore ahead of the Python sequence. The slides use fictional study hours; the notebook applies data preparation to historical stock prices. They are not a complete weekly lesson package.

| Material | Link |
| :--- | :--- |
| Lecture slides | [A first look at data](slides/01-first-data-analysis.html) |
| Guided practice | [Open Big Tech in 2022 in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/github/allanwheeler/econ3030-spring2027/blob/course-website/notebooks/01-first-data-analysis.ipynb) |
| Notebook file | [View on GitHub](https://github.com/allanwheeler/econ3030-spring2027/blob/course-website/notebooks/01-first-data-analysis.ipynb) |
| Stock-price data and definitions | [TidyTuesday source](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/main/data/2023/2023-02-07) |
| Excel practice data | [Download fictional cafe sales CSV](data/teaching/cafe-sales.csv) |

The cafe dataset describes fictional product sales by date and location. `quantity` counts items; `unit_price_usd` is dollars per item. Revenue is quantity multiplied by unit price. It contains no real people or businesses and is freely reusable.

## Tentative weekly topics

Materials will be linked here as they are released. Lab instructions remain in Canvas; Lab 1 uses Excel.

| Week | Tuesday lecture topic | Thursday guided practice | Lab materials |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | Questions, rows, columns, and Excel tables | Format, sort, and filter a table | |
| 2 | Excel formulas and cell references | Calculate a column; use SUM and AVERAGE | |
| 3 | Excel pivot tables and responsible comparisons | Summarize categories | |
| 4 | Colab, Python names, column types, and a first chart | Save and run a notebook; inspect a table and chart | |
| 5 | Selecting, filtering, and creating columns | Filter observations and compare summaries | |
| 6 | Primary keys, foreign keys, and related tables | Check identifiers and references | |
| 7 | Cardinality and joins | Predict matches and join tables | |
| 8 | Unmatched records and join validation | Check keys and row counts | |
| 9 | Grouped summaries and comparisons after joining | Pair a grouped table with a chart | |
| 10 | Missing values, duplicates, and data checks | Document cleaning decisions | |
| 11 | Distributions and unusual values | Build a histogram; compare mean and median | |
| 12 | Combining preparation, summaries, and charts | Work through a small analysis | |
| 13 | Choosing evidence for a question | Refine a summary table and two charts | |
| 14 | Writing findings and limitations | Connect evidence to claims | |
| 15 | Reproducibility and revision | Restart, run all, and review a draft | |
| 16 | Communicating a finished analysis | Final revisions and submission checks | |
